title: Microsoft Purview: archive SharePoint files from retention policies
summary: The briefing passes: its opt-in default, E5 requirement, archive storage meter and rollout dates are supported. The retention-policy route should include the final archive option, and two general retention articles need acknowledging where they disagree with the feature-specific guidance.

claims.claim: Purview Data Lifecycle Management gains retention-based archiving for SharePoint files.
claims.quote: We are introducing file archiving support in SharePoint Online, utilizing this feature administrators can seamlessly include archiving actions within their existing data retention policies.

claims.claim: The archive action is additional to keeping and deleting content.
claims.quote: in addition to keeping or deleting data, admins can now leverage Purview DLM to archive files according to organizational requirements

claims.claim: SharePoint retention labels can also carry the archive action.
claims.quote: For SharePoint, you can add an archive action to retention policies and retention labels.

claims.claim: The action moves supported inactive files to Microsoft 365 Archive.
claims.quote: This action moves supported inactive files to Microsoft 365 Archive while the files remain subject to retention and legal holds.

claims.claim: Files remain subject to retention after archiving.
claims.quote: This action moves supported inactive files to Microsoft 365 Archive while the files remain subject to retention and legal holds.

claims.claim: Files remain subject to legal holds after archiving.
claims.quote: This action moves supported inactive files to Microsoft 365 Archive while the files remain subject to retention and legal holds.

claims.claim: Archived files remain available to Microsoft Purview eDiscovery.
claims.quote: Archived files remain available for Microsoft Purview eDiscovery and content search but are excluded from Microsoft 365 Copilot indexing.

claims.claim: Archived files remain available to content search.
claims.quote: Archived files remain available for Microsoft Purview eDiscovery and content search but are excluded from Microsoft 365 Copilot indexing.

claims.claim: Existing retention policies and labels must be updated to include the archive action before they archive files.

claims.fix: Add: 'The feature-specific retention settings guidance says existing policies can be updated to add archiving; the general create-retention-policies article still says retention settings other than the retention period cannot be changed after creation.' Both https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention-settings and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-retention-policies are already cited.

claims.claim: Archived data keeps the same level of security as active data.

claims.claim: File archive actions, including policy-driven actions, are recorded as Archived file (FileArchived).
claims.quote: File archive actions are recorded in the Microsoft 365 audit log. The Archived file (FileArchived) record identifies the user or system account that archived the file.
claims.fix: Add: 'The archive-specific guidance documents FileArchived events for automatic archiving, although the general retention overview still says retention actions are audited for retention labels only, not retention policies.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention#auditing-retention-configuration-and-actions alongside the existing archive sources.

claims.claim: FileArchived identifies the user or system account that archived a file.
claims.quote: The Archived file (FileArchived) record identifies the user or system account that archived the file.

claims.claim: Configured policies archive eligible files automatically rather than requiring approval for each file.
claims.quote: To hide the Archive action from users while allowing retention policies and labels to archive eligible files automatically, run Set-SPOTenant -AllowFileArchive $false.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Learn requires a Microsoft 365 E5 licence for file-level archive.
claims.quote: File-level archive requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Licence; Open questions
claims.claim: The retention settings page says no additional setup is required to archive files using retention policies or labels.
claims.quote: No additional setup is required to archive files by using retention policies or labels.

claims.claim: The retention settings page requires pay-as-you-go setup to obtain Microsoft 365 Archive's cost-saving benefits.
claims.quote: To use the cost-saving benefits of Microsoft 365 Archive, first set up pay-as-you-go billing for Microsoft 365 Archive.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Archive uses a pay-as-you-go per-GB monthly storage meter.
claims.quote: Storage consumption is charged at a per-GB monthly rate.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The storage meter is charged only when combined archived and active SharePoint storage exceeds the tenant's included or licensed allocation.
claims.quote: This meter is charged only when archived storage plus active storage in SharePoint exceeds the included or licensed allocated SharePoint storage capacity limit of the tenant.

claims.claim: Monthly archive usage includes storage used by archived SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: Monthly archive storage usage is calculated as the total of two components: (1) the storage used by all archived SharePoint sites, and (2) the storage used by archived files that reside in non-archived SharePoint sites.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Not yet published
claims.claim: The same monthly archive meter includes archived files in non-archived SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: Monthly archive storage usage is calculated as the total of two components: (1) the storage used by all archived SharePoint sites, and (2) the storage used by archived files that reside in non-archived SharePoint sites.

claims.claim: The pricing page's billing scenarios use $0.05/GB/month.
claims.quote: Pay at $0.05/GB/month for 200 GB of archive storage.

claims.claim: The pricing model page links to a separate current price list.
claims.quote: To see the pricing for Microsoft 365 Archive, see Pay-as-you-go services and pricing.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Archive requires a linked Azure subscription for pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Before you can use Microsoft 365 Archive, you must first link your Azure subscription in pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Creating a billing policy includes an optional Budget page for a budget and alerts.
claims.quote: On the Budget page, optionally set a budget and alerts, and then select Next.

claims.claim: The archive setup page does not say that use stops at the budget.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Archive connect pay as you go billing policy API PowerShell. Read archive-setup and pay-as-you-go-setup-billing-node; setup states optional budget/alerts, not a stop. The billing-node page explicitly says reaching 100% doesn't stop service or billing.

claims.claim: Archived content remains archived if Archive is turned off or its billing is unhealthy.
claims.quote: If Microsoft 365 Archive is turned off, or if the associated archive billing subscription is unhealthy or turned off, archived content stays archived.

claims.claim: Archived content counts as active storage while Archive or billing is unavailable.
claims.quote: While Microsoft 365 Archive or billing is unavailable, archived content counts as active storage usage and counts toward standard Microsoft 365 storage consumption.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Indirect costs; Open questions
claims.claim: The pricing page says new archive actions are blocked until Archive is on and billing is healthy.
claims.quote: New archive actions are blocked until Microsoft 365 Archive is turned on and billing is healthy.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Not yet published
claims.claim: A separate rate specific to retention-based archiving is not published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Archive retention based archiving storage price separate rate. Read retention-settings, archive-pricing and syntex-pay-as-you-go-services. The published Archive meter covers files and sites; no separate retention-based rate was documented.

claims.claim: The notice names organisations using OneDrive retention policies as affected.
claims.quote: Organizations using retention policies in SharePoint Online and OneDrive

claims.where: Scope: Who and what; Open questions
claims.claim: Items that do not support the archive action remain active.
claims.quote: Items that don't support the archive action remain active.

claims.claim: Setting up Microsoft 365 Archive requires a SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator to be able to access the Microsoft 365 admin center and set up Microsoft 365 Archive.

claims.claim: Creating retention policies has separate permissions documented on the Data Lifecycle Management page linked by the retention policy article.
claims.quote: To make sure you have permissions to create and edit retention policies, see the permissions information for data lifecycle management.

claims.claim: New configurations after October 2026 use Billing > Pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: For new configurations after October 2026, connect Microsoft 365 Archive to a pay-as-you-go billing policy in Billing > Pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: The archive setup page also documents an earlier flow beginning at Settings > Org settings.
claims.quote: Turn on Microsoft 365 Archive using the earlier setup flow ... In the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Settings > Org settings.

claims.claim: The printed Purview policy route reaches the retain/delete settings page through Full directory and Static.
claims.quote: For the Assign admin units page, keep the default of Full directory. ... For the Choose the type of retention policy to create page, select Adaptive or Static ... If you chose Static: On the Choose locations page
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].ui.path and its rendered route with 'Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy > Assign admin units > Full directory > Choose the type of retention policy to create > Static > Choose locations > Decide if you want to retain content, delete it, or both > Archive retained items in secure and compliant Microsoft 365 Archive to reduce cost'. The existing cited pages https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-retention-policies and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention-settings document the route and final option.

claims.claim: An automation operation that sets the archive action on a Purview retention policy is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention SharePoint archive action PowerShell Set-RetentionComplianceRule archive parameters. Read New-RetentionComplianceRule, Set-RetentionComplianceRule and retention-settings; no documented operation sets the archive action.

claims.claim: Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Services > Microsoft 365 Archive > Connect a policy > Connection status connects an Archive billing policy.
claims.quote: go to the Services tab and find Microsoft 365 Archive. Select Connect a policy, turn on the Connection status toggle for the billing policy, and then select Save.

claims.claim: An API or command to connect Microsoft 365 Archive to a pay-as-you-go billing policy is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Archive connect pay as you go billing policy API PowerShell. Read archive-setup, pay-as-you-go-setup-billing-node and Get-BillingPolicy/New-SPOAppBillingPolicy excerpts; no operation connects Archive to a billing policy.

claims.claim: An admin UI control specifically disabling manual file archiving while preserving policy archiving is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Archive disable manual file archive admin center AllowFileArchive setting UI. Read archive-manage, archive-setup and archive-faq excerpts. Manual availability is controlled with PowerShell; the documented portal toggle enables or disables Archive itself.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -AllowFileArchive $false hides the manual Archive action tenant-wide.
claims.quote: set the -AllowFileArchive property of the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet to False. This tenant setting overrides the site-level property with the same name and blocks manual file archiving across the tenant.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls prose; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Disabling manual file archiving does not prevent admin-defined policies from automatically archiving eligible files.
claims.quote: Admins can remove the Archive action from users while continuing to use admin-defined policies to archive eligible files automatically.

claims.claim: A SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator can control manual file archiving.
claims.quote: SharePoint Administrators or Global Administrators can control manual file archiving for all SharePoint sites, a subset of sites, or not at all.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -AllowFileArchive controls manual archiving on individual sites.
claims.quote: Site-level manual archiving. To control which sites show the Archive action to users, use the -AllowFileArchive property of the Set-SPOSite cmdlet.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -AllowFileArchiveOnNewSitesByDefault controls manual archiving defaults for new sites.
claims.quote: To control whether users can manually archive files on sites created in the future, use the -AllowFileArchiveOnNewSitesByDefault property of the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet.

claims.claim: Get-SPOSite exposes ArchivedFileDiskUsed to report archived file storage on a site.
claims.quote: The 'ArchivedFileDiskUsed' property of the Get-SPOSite cmdlet indicates the storage consumed by all archived files on that site in bytes.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search reaches audit search.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations FileArchived searches the unified audit log for file archive operations.
claims.quote: The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation. ... For a list of the available values for this parameter, see Audited activities.

claims.claim: Audit search requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs permissions.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log. ... To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining the E5 entitlement with Archive consumption billing.
claims.quote: File-level archive requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license. ... To use the cost-saving benefits of Microsoft 365 Archive, first set up pay-as-you-go billing for Microsoft 365 Archive.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog must be run in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: FileArchived audit events can identify which automatic policy archived a file.
claims.quote: When an automatic file archive policy archives a file, the event includes the policy ID, policy version, and the file's last access date.

claims.claim: The retention settings page states the E5 requirement without specifying which users or sites must hold it.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview retention based file archiving Microsoft 365 E5 licensing supported items price. Read retention-settings and Purview service-description excerpts. The feature section gives E5 but no assignment detail; general retention licensing guidance exists separately.

claims.claim: The retention settings page does not list the items that do not support the archive action.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview retention based file archiving Microsoft 365 E5 licensing supported items price. Read retention-settings and archive-overview. The former says unsupported items remain active without listing them; the latter separately lists file-archive limitations.

claims.claim: The notice recommends reviewing current retention policies.
claims.quote: Review your current retention policies in Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management.

claims.claim: Administrators configure the archive action on individual retention policies within the tenant.
claims.quote: For SharePoint, you can add an archive action to retention policies and retention labels. ... To configure the archive action, select Archive retained items in secure and compliant Microsoft 365 Archive to reduce cost in the retention settings.

claims.claim: The notice recommends evaluating opportunities to reduce storage costs by archiving inactive content.
claims.quote: Evaluate opportunities to reduce storage costs by archiving inactive content.
